newsitem.title: USA: Latin America to get advanced US arms more easily.
newsitem.headline: Latin America to get advanced US arms more easily.

text.p: President Bill Clinton, altering a 20-year-old policy, has decided to make it easier for Latin American countries to buy advanced U.S. arms, U.S. officials said on Friday.

"In the past there's a been a presumption of denial" when Latin American governments wanted to purchase American-made weapons, a senior official told Reuters. But now Clinton was "lifting that presumption of denial," the official said.
This decision, a change of policy not law, effectively "puts Latin America into the same category as the rest of the world, which is to say we examine each case on the merits," he said.
The Carter administration adopted the policy, which amounted to an effective ban on arms sales to Latin America, during an era when most of the region was under military rule.

But now, the senior official said, "Latin America has become like the rest of the world." Most countries on the continent are democracies with their armed forces largely under civilian control, and they have good relations with their neighbours, the official added.
